headline: Stocks are bouncing in today's half-day Black Friday session after a rough Wednesday. Bonds are pulling the other way: hot October inflation has markets pricing a near-certain Fed hike on Dec 9, pushing the 10-year back above 4.9% and holding the dollar at its highs.
highlights: Rally, but the trends are still bearish. By late morning the S&P 500 was up about 1.4% near 7,282 and the Nasdaq about 1.9%. Tech led, Amazon rose about 4% on strong Black Friday demand, and Adobe counted about $7.1B in Thanksgiving Day online sales, up 10.4% from last year. Breadth is strong: 81.1% of stocks are up and no sector is down. Even so, SPY (728.32) and QQQ (650.99) are still in Bearish trends, sitting inside their ranges below the 741.33 and 669.6 sell levels. AMZN (254.12) is still Bearish, while TSLA turned Bullish today at 400.00, just under its 408.24 sell level.

The Fed is on track to hike. October core PCE, the Fed's preferred gauge, rose to 3.3% year over year against 3.2% expected, the highest in 3 years. Headline PCE came in at 3.8%. Minutes from the last Fed meeting said almost all officials think further hikes would likely be appropriate. As of Nov 26, swap-market pricing put the chance of a 0.25-point hike on Dec 9 at 96%, which would lift the 4.00% upper bound to 4.25%. Fed officials go quiet before the Dec 8–9 meeting, so the data, not Fed speeches, will move expectations next week.

Rates and the dollar are pushing back against the rally. The 10-year yield rose more than 6 bps to about 4.91–4.93%, in line with the dashboard's 4.91%. The 2-year is near 4.68–4.70%, and the dashboard's 10y–2y spread is +24 bps. The Dollar Index is about 104.0, which the dashboard flags as AT HIGHS. UUP (29.72) is Bullish and sits just under its 29.78 sell level, while FXE (100.98) stays Bearish. The strong dollar is one of three items still keeping the bottom checklist at 5/8.

Volatility has calmed but credit hasn't confirmed. Wednesday was very choppy: new tariff proposals and a sharp AI selloff took the S&P 500 down 3.2% at its intraday low before it closed 0.3% lower at 7,182.78. The VIX closed that day at 27.17 and is now 23.81, a fast drop below 25. Junk-bond spreads at 377 bps are still VOLATILE, up 51 bps in 20 days, and HYG (76.61) is Bearish between 76.08 and 76.83. The checklist also still lacks a 90% up day; the last 90% down day was Nov 19.

Strong growth and jobs data keep the Fed leaning toward hikes. Initial jobless claims fell to 189K, matching the lowest since 1969, and Q3 GDP is at a revised 4.3% annualized. A hot economy with inflation rising helps explain why the defensive sectors hold Bullish trends: XLU 43.73, XLP 92.68 and XLV 184.2. XLRE (44.14) is also Bullish despite a near-4.9% 10-year. Cyclical sectors XLI (165.56) and XLE (61.67) remain Bearish.

Commodities are mixed. Gold rose more than 1.6% to about $3,633 despite higher yields and a stronger dollar. On the dashboard, GLD (334.4) is still Bearish below its 341.4 sell level and GDX (79.18) is just under its 79.55 sell level. WTI crude was about $84.47 early, up 0.9%, but USO (137.77) has been Bearish since Nov 9.

releases.read: Hotter than expected and the highest in 3 years. Core prices rose 0.3% for the month, and the 3-month annualized pace is 3.6%. This locks in December hike expectations.
In line with forecasts, but September was revised higher. The monthly rise slowed to 0.3% from 0.5%. Real spending was roughly flat, and the saving rate rose to 4.1%.
Better than expected, matching the year's low and the lowest since 1969. Continuing claims fell 95K to 1.70M. The labor market looks too tight for the Fed to stop hiking.
Shows a resilient economy. With strong growth and core inflation at 3.3%, the Fed has little reason to stop hiking.
Turned positive, adding to signs of firm factory activity ahead of next week's ISM report.

upcoming.why: First regional reading of the week. A firm print would support the strong-growth story weighing on QQQ and IWM.
Expected to cool slightly. It's also an energy-region read while XLE and USO are in Bearish trends.
Still well into expansion. A strong prices-paid reading would add to inflation worries and the pressure on yields with the 10-year at 4.91%.
First private-payrolls read before Friday's jobs report, with the Fed's blackout period limiting other signals.
Claims near 57-year lows have supported hike pricing. A move up would be the first sign of the job market easing.
Services drive core inflation, so watch the prices component given core PCE at 3.3%.
The last big data point before the Dec 8–9 Fed meeting. A second strong month could revive talk of a 0.5-point hike and test the rebound in SPY and QQQ.

upcoming.why: Inflation expectations in this survey matter with headline PCE at 3.8% and Black Friday spending in focus for XLY and AMZN.
